rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses steadfastness as affirming God's oneness, obeying Him, and adhering to the Prophet's Sunna.
rows.anchor: وحدوا الله، واستقاموا: عملوا بطاعته ولزموا سنة نبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels give them glad tidings at death and at resurrection, so the terrors of the Resurrection do not frighten them.
rows.anchor: يبشرونهم عند الموت وفي وقت البعث فلا تهولهم أهوال القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are promised Paradise, which they will enter as a lodging or welcome gift.
rows.anchor: معناه وأبشروا بالجنة تنزلونها نزلا

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash parses naẓulan as an accusative verbal noun, with the sense that what they desire has been sent down for them as a sending-down.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الأخفش: (نزلا) منصوب من وجهين:

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash also allows naẓulan as a circumstantial accusative, meaning the desired things are sent down as a lodging, like saying Zayd came walking for Zayd came walking on foot.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا على الحال على معنى لكم فيها ما تشتهي أنفسكم منزلا نزلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase man aḥsanu qawlan is an accusative of specification, like saying Zayd is better than you in face.
rows.anchor: منصوب على التفسير كما تقول زيد أحسن منك وجها

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: One tafsir identifies the caller to God as Muhammad, because he called people to God's oneness.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أنه يعنى به محمد

rows.speaker: عائشة وغيرها
rows.claim: A report from Aisha and others says the verse was revealed about the callers to prayer.
rows.anchor: وجاء أيضا في التفسير عن عائشة وغيرها أنها نزلت في المؤذنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second lā is emphatic and extra; the sense is that good and evil are not equal.
rows.anchor: زائدة مؤكدة، المعنى لا تستوي والسيئة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to repel an evil deed with what is better.
rows.anchor: معناه ادفع السيئة بالتي هي أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīm means a close relative or intimate.
rows.anchor: (كأنه ولي حميم): الحميم القريب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to receiving the recompense for this virtuous act, or to receiving the act itself.
rows.anchor: أي ما يلقى مجازاة هذا أي وما يلقى هذه الفعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who receive it are the patient ones who restrain their anger.
rows.anchor:
الذين صبروا) أي
إلا الذين يكظمون الغيظ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great portion is Paradise, which only those for whom Paradise is due will receive.
rows.anchor: الحظ ههنا الجنة، أي وما يلقاها إلا من وجبت له الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A great portion means a great share in goodness.
rows.anchor: أي حظ عظيم في الخير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Satan whispers something that turns a person away from forbearance, they should seek refuge in God.
rows.anchor: إن نزغك من الشيطان ما يصرفك به عن الاحتمال فاستعذ بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing in every created thing may refer to male and female in animals, as also stated in 53:45.
rows.anchor: على الحيوان لأن الذكر والأنثى يقال لهما زوجان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows pairs to mean two kinds in everything: male and female among animals, and two categories among other living and inanimate things.
rows.anchor: صنفان أصل كل حيوان وموات، والله أعلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Flee to God from associating partners with Him and from disobeying Him; the warning is of His punishment.
rows.anchor: المعنى ففروا إلى الله من الشرك بالله ومن معاصيه إليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The situation is the same as before: earlier peoples also denied the messengers.
rows.anchor: المعنى الأمر كذلك، أي كما فعل من قبلهم في تكذيب الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In saying every messenger was called a sorcerer, huwa is understood before sāḥir, so the phrase means, 'They said: this is a sorcerer.'
rows.anchor: أي إلا قالوا هذا ساحر، ارتفع ساحر بإضمار هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first people advised the last to say the same thing; the opening hamza is both reproach and interrogation.
rows.anchor: معناه أوصى أولهم آخرهم، وهذه ألف التوبيخ وألف الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no blame on the Prophet once he has delivered the message.
rows.anchor: أي لا لوم عليك إذ أديت الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder should recall God's days, punishment, retribution, and mercy.
rows.anchor: أي ذكرهم بأيام الله وعذابه وعقابه ورحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God already knew before creating jinn and humans which would worship Him and which would disbelieve; creation therefore does not mean coercing everyone into worship, since that would leave no disbelievers.
rows.anchor: الله - عز وجل - قد علم من قبل أن يخلق الجن والإنس من يعبده ممن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the purpose as calling the jinn and humans to worship, intending worship from those fit for it.
rows.anchor: وأنا مريد العبادة منهم، يعني من أهلها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not want them to provide for or feed anyone, since He is the Provider and Feeder.
rows.anchor: أي ما أريد أن يرزقوا أحدا من عبادي، وما أريد أن يطعموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading al-matīn is better Arabic because it makes 'the Firm' an adjective of God.
rows.anchor: والقراءة الرفع وهو في العربية أحسن نكون رفع (المتين) صفة لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive reading makes al-matīn an adjective of al-quwwa, treating feminine quwwa like feminine mawʿiẓa.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (ذو القوة المتين) - بالخفض - جعل المتين صفة للقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example 'whoever receives an admonition' shows that a feminine noun can be used with this kind of construction.
rows.anchor: كما قال: (فمن جاءه موعظة)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhū al-quwwa al-matīn means the possessor of mighty power.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (ذو القوة المتين) ذو [الاقتدار] الشديد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised the sky above the earth and held it so that it would not fall onto the earth.
rows.anchor: المعنى رفعها فوق الأرض وأمسكها أن تقع على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He established the balance so that people could settle disputes fairly with one another.
rows.anchor: ووضع الميزان لينتصف بعض الناس من بعض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation takes the balance as justice, since equating things is a kind of balancing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الميزان ههنا العدل، لأن المعادلة موازنة الأشياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not transgressing in the balance means not exceeding its proper measure and justice.
rows.anchor:
(ألا تطغوا في الميزان (8)
ألا يجاوزوا القدر والعدل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be construed as a purpose clause: 'so that you do not transgress in the balance.'
rows.anchor: ويجوز (ألا تطغوا) بمعنى اللام، " لأن لا تطغوا "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a prohibition, with an serving as explanatory, meaning God set the balance by saying not to transgress in it.
rows.anchor: وتكون (ألا تطغوا) على النهي ومعنى " أن " التفسير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following command to establish fair weight and not diminish the balance supports taking the preceding words as a prohibition against transgression.
rows.anchor:
ويدل عليه المعطوف عليه وهو قوله:
(وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ولا تخسروا الميزان (9)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted reading has ḍamma on the tāʾ; Arabic allows both akhsartu al-mīzān and khasirtu al-mīzān, with the latter corresponding to the form in the verse.
rows.anchor: القراءة بضم التاء، وروى أهل اللغة: أخسرت الميزان وخسرت، فعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not adopt the alternative reading without a sound report from a recognized reading authority; an unnamed early reader was not a source for recitation.
rows.anchor:
ولا تقرأن بها إلا أن تثبت رواية صحيحة عن إمام في القراءة.
وقد روي أن إنسانا قرأ بها من المتقدمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the opening construction, the first al-ḥāqqa is a subject, mā is another subject, and the second al-ḥāqqa predicates mā and refers back to it.
rows.anchor: الأولة: مرفوع بالابتداء، و " ما " رفع بالابتداء أيضا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question form magnifies the event's significance, as in asking 'Zayd, what is he?' to exalt or disparage him.
rows.anchor: على تقدير ما هي، والمعنى تفخيم شأنها، واللفظ لفظ استفهام كما تقول: زيد ما هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥāqqa means the Hour or Resurrection; it is so named because every good or evil deed a person does becomes real and established.
rows.anchor: والحاقة: الساعة والقيامة وسميت (الحاقة) لأنها تحق كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'What could make you know what the Reality is?' asks what thing could inform the hearer about the Reality.
rows.anchor: معناه أي شيء أعلمك ما الحاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative mā is nominative despite following adrāka, because a word in an interrogative construction is not governed by what precedes it.
rows.anchor: لأن ما كان في لفظ الاستفهام لا يعمل فيه ما قبله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qāriʿa here means the Resurrection.
rows.anchor:
(كذبت ثمود وعاد بالقارعة (4)
أي بالقيامة.

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Language authorities explain bi-l-ṭāghiya as 'because of their transgression'; the form fāʿila can serve as a verbal noun, like ʿāfiya or ʿāqiba.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (بالطاغية) عند أهل اللغة بطغيانهم، وفاعلة قد يأتي يمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's sense points to their destruction by an overwhelming quake, rather than merely by their own transgression.
rows.anchor: والذي يدل عليه معنى الآية. - والله أعلم - أنهم أهلكوا بالرجفة الطاغية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A very great thing can be called ʿāt or ʿātiya; the description of ʿĀd's fierce wind supports this usage for the overwhelming event.
rows.anchor: يقال للشيء العظيم عات وعاتية، وكذلك أهلكوا بالطاغية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water that exceeded its proper level is described as transgressing, illustrating how the word conveys excess in magnitude.
rows.anchor: فوصف الماء بالطغيان لمجاوزته القدر في الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided the human being to the path, either toward wretchedness or toward happiness.
rows.anchor: معناه هديناه الطريق إما لشقوة وإما لسعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, salāsil would best be left diptote, but it is declinable here to keep the verse endings in one form.
rows.anchor:
الأجود في العربية ألا يصرف سلاسل، ولكن لما جعلت رأس آية
صرفت ليكون آخر الآي على لفظ واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular of abrār is barr.
rows.anchor: الأبرار واحدهم بر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible meaning is that the drink's pleasant flavor is camphor.
rows.anchor: في اللغة أن يكون طعم الطيب فيها والكافور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the drink may actually be mixed with camphor; that causes no harm because Paradise's inhabitants suffer neither harm nor fatigue.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يمزج بالكافور فلا يكون في ذلك ضرر لأن أهل الجنة لا يمسهم فيما يأكلون ويشربون ضرر ولا نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, a kaʾs is a vessel containing drink; without drink in it, it is not called a cup.
rows.anchor:
والكأس في اللغة الإناء إذا كان فيه الشراب.
فإذا لم يكن فيه الشراب لم يسم كأسا.

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The anonymous poetic citation uses the word kaʾs for a drinking vessel; the witnessed word is al-kaʾs.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: صبنت الكأس عنا أم عمرو وكان الكأس مجراها اليمينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl is nominative as a subject, with li-l-muṭaffifīn as its predicate; nominative is best because their doom is already fixed.
rows.anchor: (ويل) رفع بالابتداء والخبر قوله (للمطففين)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outside the Qur'an, waylan in the accusative would mean that God assigned them a doom; the Qur'anic wording cannot be changed against the written text.
rows.anchor:
ولو كان في غير القرآن لجاز
" ويلا " للمطففين، على معنى جعل الله لهم ويلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl is an expression used for anyone in punishment and ruin.
rows.anchor: والويل كلمة تقال لكل من هو في عذاب وهلكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muṭaffifūn are people who give short measure or weight.
rows.anchor: والمطففون الذين ينقصون المكيال والميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name comes from taking only a tiny amount in measure or weight, from ṭaff, the edge of something.
rows.anchor: وإنما أخذ من طف الشيء وهو جانبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they measure from others, they demand the full measure; likewise, when they buy by weight, they demand full weight.
rows.anchor: إذا اكتالوا من الناس استوفوا عليهم الكيل وكذلك إذا اتزنوا استوفوا الوزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not separately mention their weighing when buying because buying and selling involve goods measured or weighed.
rows.anchor: والوزن بهما الشراء والبيع فيما يكال ويوزن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they measure or weigh for other people, they reduce the amount given.
rows.anchor: أي إذا كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم يخسرون، أي ينقصون في الكيل والوزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic permits the form yukh'sirūn here, although he knows of no one who recited that form in this place.
rows.anchor: ولا أعلم أحدا قرأ في هذا الموضع يخسرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred parse, the pronoun in kālūhum is an object meaning 'they measured for them'; it must be joined to the verb, so one cannot pause after kālū.
rows.anchor: لم يجز أن يقف على كالوا حتى يصلها ب (هم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some treat hum as emphasis for the subject pronoun in kālū, which would permit pausing after the verb.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من يجعل " هم " توكيدا لما في كالوا، فيجوز أن تقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers parsing hum as an accusative object meaning 'for them'; if it were emphasis, the written text would contain an alif before hum.
rows.anchor: والاختيار أن تكون " هم " في موضع نصب، بمعنى كالوا لهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great day is the Resurrection; if the defrauders believed they would be resurrected, they would not cheat in measure or weight.
rows.anchor: يعنى يوم القيامة، أي إنهم لو ظنوا أنهم يبعثون ما نقصوا في الكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the transmitted reading, yawm is accusative and governed by mabʿūthūn: they are resurrected on the day people stand before the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor:
(يوم) منصوب بقوله (مبعوثون)
المعنى ألا يظنون أنهم يبعثون يوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A genitive reading of yawm would also be good Arabic, with the meaning 'for the day when people stand.'
rows.anchor:
ولو قرئت " يوم يقوم الناس "
بكسر يوم لكان جيدا على معنى ليوم يقوم الناس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nominative reading would also be good Arabic, meaning 'that is the day when people stand.'
rows.anchor: ولو قرئت بالرفع لكان جيدا يوم يقوم الناس، على معنى ذلك يوم يقوم الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These syntactically possible alternatives should not be recited unless transmitted by the reciters, because recitation is a received practice and Arabic possibility alone does not authorize a change.
rows.anchor:
ولا يجوز القراءة إلا بما قرأ به القراء
(يوم يقوم الناس) - بالنصب -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā is a rebuke and alert; the sense is that matters are not as the wrongdoers suppose, so they should desist.
rows.anchor:
(كلا) ردع وتنبيه.
المعنى ليس الأمر على ما هم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl is nominative as a subject and li-kulli hamaza is its predicate; this is better Arabic because doom is already fixed for them.
rows.anchor:
(ويل) مرفوع بالابتداء والخبر (لكل همزة)
ولو كان في غير القرآن جاز النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An accusative waylan is possible outside the Qur'an, meaning that God assigned them a doom, but that form is excluded by the written text.
rows.anchor: ولو كان في غير القرآن جاز النصب، ولا يجوز في القرآن لمخالفة المصحف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl is an expression for anyone who has fallen into ruin.
rows.anchor: والويل كلمة تقال لكل من وقع في هلكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hamaza-lamaza is someone who backbites people and insults or derides them.
rows.anchor: والهمزة اللمزة الذي يغتاب الناس ويغضهم

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The anonymous poetic line uses al-hāmiz al-lamza for a backbiter and mocker; these are the words it witnesses.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: إذا لقيتك عن كره تكاشرني. . . وإن تغيبت كنت الهامز اللمزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for collecting wealth is reported with a light and a doubled consonant reading.
rows.anchor: وقرئت: (الذي جمع مالا)، وقرئت (جمع مالا)، بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ʿaddadahu is read with the consonant doubled or lightened.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (وعدده) بالتشديد، وقرئت (وعدده) - بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the doubled reading, he counted or kept counting the wealth over long stretches of time.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ (وعدده) فمعناه، وعدده للدهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the light reading, he collected wealth and numbers, meaning a group of people he prepared as supporters.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (وعدده) فمعناه جمع مالا وعددا، أي وقوما أعدهم نصارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He acts like a wealthy person who does not think that he will die, as if his wealth made him immortal.
rows.anchor: أي يعمل عمل من لا يظن مع يساره أنه يموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will be cast into the Fire; al-ḥuṭama is one of the names of Hell.
rows.anchor: والحطمة اسم من أسماء النار.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to recite linbudhāni, meaning that the man and his wealth will both be cast into the Fire.
rows.anchor: ورويت - عن الحسن، على أن المعنى لينبذن هو وماله في الحطمة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading, latunbadhanna, means that he and what he amassed will be cast into the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (لتنبذن) في الحطمة، فمعناه أنه لينبذ هو وجمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar reading is lanbudhanna.
rows.anchor:
في
الحطمة. والقراءة المعروفة (لينبذن).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's kindled Fire is prepared for these disbelievers and anyone like them.
rows.anchor: هذه نار معدة لهؤلاء الكفار ومن كان مثلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire reaching the hearts means its pain and burning reach the hearts.
rows.anchor: يبلغ ألمها وإحراقها إلى الأفئدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for being closed is read both with and without hamza; Arabic has the forms awṣadtuhu and āṣadtuhu, respectively.
rows.anchor:
قرئت بالهمز وبغير همز.
وقرئت موصدة، والعرب تقول أوصدته فعلى هذا موصدة.
وتقول آصدته فعلى هذا مؤصدة. بالهمزة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mūṣada means shut or covered over; the punishment is closed around them.
rows.anchor: ومعنى " موصدة " مطبقة، أي العذاب مطبق عليهم.
